newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines posts below-normal rainfall in June.
newsitem.headline: Philippines posts below-normal rainfall in June.

text.p: Eighty percent of the Philippines experienced below-normal rainfall in June despite the supposed onset of the rainy season, a local climate expert said on Friday.

Philippine Atmospheric Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) climatology chief Aida Jose told reporters the southern part of the main Luzon island and eastern part of the country registered only 40 percent of the normal rainfall level last month.
The southern Mindanao island, which is one of the major food producer, also suffered from lower level of rainfall.
Jose attributed the dry situation to the onset of the El Nino phenomenon, a prolonged dry season which have been recurring in the country since the early 1990s.
The El Nino phenomenon is expected to peak in the second half of the year and extend to the early part of 1998, she added.
Tropical storms, which average about 20 every year, will be less in evidence this year. As of the end of May, only four storms have visited the country.
The Department of Agriculture recently said it had prepared for the prolonged dry season by improving the irrigation system and stocking enough food supply.
